fact: GRAIN's study says none of the four countries, Senegal included, has an AI-specific law or mandatory mechanisms for algorithmic transparency, audit or redress for AI discrimination.
Senegal's Commission de protection des donnees personnelles (CDP) condemns AI-generated manipulated content and deep fakes and says their authors are exposed to sanctions provided by law.

fact: Senegal's CDP said on 5 November 2026 that recording or reproducing a person's voice or image by AI without legal basis is unlawful processing under Law 2008-12.

La Tribune Afrique reports that the National Assembly adopted bill 04/2026 creating the CNRM on 3 March 2026, which charges it with overseeing transparency of AI-generated content; no promulgation or entry into force is stated.

APS reports that CDP president Ousmane Thiongane said a workshop was upgrading a personal-data bill and implementing decree that the CDP wants to present, framed as a response to new threats from AI, robotics and big data.
